title: I Fixed The Bug. Then My Pipeline Refused to Run.
why_read: A practical post-mortem about a confusing CI/CD pipeline failure caused by exhausted compute minutes rather than actual code errors, useful for engineers who've hit similarly opaque pipeline issues.
analysis: This is a troubleshooting narrative about a GitLab CI/CD pipeline that failed with no logs and no clear error, eventually traced to running out of allotted compute minutes rather than any code or infrastructure problem. It's a useful reminder that pipeline failures aren't always caused by the code being tested, and that infrastructure quotas can silently block execution with misleading symptoms. The post is written as a practical debugging story rather than a deep technical dive, but it offers a concrete lesson that could save other engineers time when they hit a similar dead-end. It's a modest but genuinely useful addition for engineers who work with CI/CD systems regularly.
